task: listwise ranking of the legal turns available at one root, so that a shortlist of fixed size contains the turns the expensive evaluation would have chosen

teacher.note: the champion's own expensive evaluation; the student exists to choose which candidates get it

model.output_rationale: an ordering is invariant to monotone transforms, so there is nothing to calibrate; a sigmoid would compress exactly the distinctions the ranker exists to make, and `contracts.prerank` refuses a calibration block for the same reason
model.capacity_rationale: narrower than the evaluator's 64x64 because this runs on every legal turn before the search consults its deadline, and the schema was already chosen for cost; 9 inputs do not need more
model.feature_standardisation: train-statistics, carried inside the model as a constant affine transform so the serving contract keeps taking raw features

loss.name: listnet-cross-entropy

target_distribution.rank: 1-based rank of the candidate's target within its group, descending, ties at the average rank
target_distribution.normalisation: gains divided by their sum within the group
rationale: the mass sits where the metric looks: the search rescores every shortlisted candidate with the expensive evaluation and takes the best, so the only candidate that has to survive the cut is the maximum, and an inverse-square discount holds 98.8% of the target mass inside the top 48 at every group size the corpus has

the shape does not move with the list's length: the best candidate carries 0.608 of the mass at 61 candidates and at 2,420 alike, so a long list teaches the same lesson about its top few as a short one

scale-free: targets are in the teacher's private units and their spread varies by orders of magnitude between groups, which a softmax over raw values would turn into a per-group temperature nobody chose
sentinel-free: a king capture carries TerminalWinScore (2^31-1) and no magnitude is used, so the sentinel ranks first and needs no mapping
tie-honest: a group whose candidates all score the same becomes a uniform target, which asks the model to be flat there rather than to invent an order

rejected_before_any_run.note: the NDCG discount was written into this protocol first and measured out of it before the model was trained even once; the numbers below are properties of the gain function, not results
rejected_before_any_run.why_not_log: on the large groups, the only ones the metric is measured on, it is barely distinguishable from not ranking at all
rejected_before_any_run.why_not_harmonic: it makes the best candidate of a long list worth half of the best candidate of a short one, weighting the hard groups down exactly when they matter most
rejected_before_any_run.why_not_one_hot: it is the limit of this family and says nothing about the rest of the ordering; the inverse square keeps a graded head (0.61, 0.15, 0.07, 0.04) while still spending almost nothing outside the shortlist

loss.groups_used: every group with two or more candidates; a single-candidate group has no ordering to learn

split.unit: whole group; a root's own candidates are the thing being ordered and cannot be split
split.leakage_note: a root occurs once in a corpus by construction, because its group id is derived from its position and roll

definitions.recall_at_k: share of evaluated groups in which some candidate holding the teacher's maximum target is inside the student's top K
definitions.rank1: share in which the student's own top candidate holds the teacher's maximum target
definitions.ndcg_at_k: normalised discounted cumulative gain at K over the same gains the loss uses

metrics.k_rationale: the production candidateLimit of the champion's search
metrics.evaluated_groups: only groups with more than K candidates
metrics.evaluated_groups_rationale: in a group no larger than the shortlist every candidate survives and the ranker cannot be wrong; including those groups would flatter every figure by the share of the corpus they make up, which in the first corpus is 45%
metrics.tie_policy: by target value, never by index: a group can have several candidates holding the maximum

material_diff.definition: order candidates by the `material_diff` column, descending
material_diff.why: this is the engine's shipped pre-ranker — `ExpectimaxSearch.materialBatch` — and it is computable from the corpus without a second label, so the question 'is a learned ranker worth anything' has an answer from the same data

random.definition: order candidates by a seeded permutation
random.why: a lower bound; recall at K of a random order is about K/N, which says how much of any result is the shortlist being generous rather than the ranker being right

not_available.cheap_score: the champion's own phase-1 ranker, `HunterEval.cheapScore`, is the ranker a learned model would actually replace in that bot, and it is a stronger baseline than material alone. The corpus carries only the expensive target, so it cannot be measured here; adding it is a change to the dataset contract and a regeneration, not a tuning decision.

admissibility.rationale: the ablation of #17 produced arms worse than a constant and only a floor caught it; a learned ranker that does not beat the ordering the engine already ships is a negative result to report, not a starting point to tune from

uncertainty.status: deferred to the metrics work; this protocol fixes the definition so the later numbers are comparable

deferred: ndcg_at_k and bootstrap intervals — reported by the metrics work, defined here so they cannot be chosen after seeing a result
serving latency at the seam, which decides whether the capacity above is affordable
a fixed-time arena, which is the only thing that can say the ranker makes the bot stronger rather than more accurate
